# PwC accelerates enterprise-scale GenAI adoption with CrewAI
Case studyProfessional Services / Enterprise AI ConsultingFortune 500 Enterprise
Details Interviewee
    Jacob Wilson Company
    PwC Industry
    Professional Services / Enterprise AI Consulting Sector
    Fortune 500 Enterprise Application
    
Code-generation & SDLC automation, Long-form functional / technical spec drafting, Real-time validation & log analysis, Agent performance monitoring & ROI analytics
## PwC Accelerates enterprise-scale GenAI adoption with CrewAI
Efficiency Gains
> _We went from roughly 10% accuracy on code generation to 70%+ once we brought Crew AI agents into the workflow.”_
PwC consultants needed faster, more-accurate generation of proprietary-language code and lengthy spec documents. Early Gen-AI prototypes lacked real-time feedback, produced inconsistent results (~10% accuracy), and offered little transparency into ROI—undermining user trust.
#### Background Context
PwC began a firm-wide Gen-AI transformation two years ago, initially building its own plug-in framework. As use-case complexity grew, the team paused to reassess tools that could boost accuracy and deliver better user experiences without steep learning curves.
#### Why They Chose Us
Crew AI offered a low barrier to entry for non-expert developers yet allowed deep API customization for advanced teams. Native agent-monitoring integrations gave PwC unprecedented visibility into task durations, tool selection, and human-versus-agent effort—crucial for demonstrating ROI.‍
#### Implementation Overview
  * Re-engineered SDLC workflows with Crew AI agents that generate, execute, and iteratively validate proprietary-language code.
  * Embedded agents to draft and refine long functional & technical specifications with real-time consultant feedback loops.
  * Leveraged Crew AI’s monitoring stack to track agent choices, run times, and accuracy, feeding KPI dashboards for leadership.


#### Results Summary
Crew-powered agents boosted code-generation accuracy from 10% to 70%, slashed turnaround time on complex documents, and supplied granular data to prove ROI. Enhanced accuracy and user experience restored consultant trust, accelerating adoption of agentic solutions across PwC.

# IBM automates federal eligibility with Agents
Case studyConsulting for Federal GovernmentEnterprise (Fortune 500)
Details Interviewee
    Narayanan Alavandar Company
    IBM Consulting ​(Federal) Industry
    Consulting for Federal Government Sector
    Enterprise (Fortune 500) Application
    
Applicant‑eligibility determination, Document extraction & summarization, Business‑rule orchestration / intelligent automation, RPA‑to‑AI agent migration
## IBM Automates federal eligibility with Agents
> _We use Crew AI basically to determine the eligibility of an applicant... we use flows—that’s what gives us flexibility!”_
#### Challenge
Federal agencies face an aging workforce and decades‑old legacy systems, making it difficult to process critical applications quickly and cost‑effectively. Coordinating multiple synchronous and asynchronous systems with traditional RPA tools left gaps in speed, scalability, and business‑rule control. ​
After 24 years at IBM—and seven spent building AI‑automation platforms for U.S. federal clients—Naran began exploring multi‑agent frameworks in 2024. By 2025 his team had two CrewAI pilots running inside federal agencies, integrated with IBM’s WatsonX foundation‑model runtime. ​
CrewAI offered a hands‑on, open‑source framework that matured rapidly, let architects blend AI agents with custom code and business rules, and integrated cleanly with WatsonX. Strong support from the CrewAI team convinced IBM Consulting to pursue an enterprise license for multiple federal deals.
In implementation, Naran & team:​
  * Built a hybrid “AI Flows + Crew Agents” architecture to control when rules‑based decisions versus autonomous agents run.
  * Deployed multiple agents to extract applicant data from documents, summarize findings, and calculate program eligibility.
  * Integrated CrewAI with WatsonX.AI to leverage IBM’s foundation‑model runtime while coordinating legacy and modern systems.


Early pilots show faster, more efficient eligibility determinations than legacy RPA—reducing manual coordination across disparate systems. IBM Consulting is finalizing enterprise‑license deals with federal agencies, aiming to move the pilots into full production and scale intelligent automation government‑wide.

## AWS powers bedrock Agents with CrewAI
Efficiency Gains
> _I would highly recommend getting started with … CrewAI’s framework—it’s a very easy‑to‑understand way to see what agents are capable of."_
#### Partnership Overview
As generative‑AI agents shift from demo toys to mission‑critical software, AWS and CrewAI partnered to help enterprises design, govern, and scale autonomous systems that stay within strict security and compliance guardrails—bridging the mindset gap between rules‑based apps and self‑directed agents.
CrewAI’s open‑source “flows‑and‑crews” architecture plugs straight into Bedrock models and AWS monitoring, giving enterprises a secure, modular, and vendor‑neutral foundation for large‑scale intelligent automation.
As a part of the joining of forces, we:‍
  * Published reference blueprints mapping CrewAI agents to Bedrock FMs, memory, and guardrails.
  * Open‑sourced exemplar systems—e.g., a multi‑agent AWS security audit crew, legacy‑code modernization flows, and CPG back‑office automation.
  * Embedded observability (CloudWatch, AgentOps, LangFuse) so customers can trace, debug, and harden agents from POC to production.


Early pilots show concrete ROI: a Fortune‑scale code‑modernization project ran ~70% faster, while a CPG back‑office flow cut processing time by 90%. The partnership is now guiding a growing pipeline of Bedrock‑powered agent rollouts as enterprises race to capitalize on the agentic trend.

# Gelato accelerates fulfillment via agentic integration
Case studyOn‑Demand Manufacturing & Logistics Platform (Creator Economy)E-Commerce
Details Interviewee

Bulk product‑SKU data mapping, Local print‑on‑demand fulfillment & logistics, Carrier onboarding / supply‑chain integration, Internal workflow & efficiency automatio
## Gelato accelerates fulfillment via agentic integration
Efficiency Gains
> _We can now integrate a new carrier in 10 minutes that used to take us 5 days.” ​_
#### Challenge
Printers joining Gelato’s network had to manually map as many as 200,000 SKUs, a task that previously took 9–24 months and often stalled, costing both sides revenue. Internally, adding new logistics carriers required days of engineering effort, slowing global expansion. ​ ​
#### Background Context
With 250 staff spread across 50 countries, Gelato set out to scale its “produce‑locally, sell‑globally” platform without linearly expanding headcount. The product team saw multi‑agent AI as the lever to remove manual bottlenecks and let each employee—and customer—do more, faster. ​
CrewAI’s agent framework could plug into Gelato Connect, automating heavy data‑mapping and integration work while remaining invisible to end‑users—freeing engineers to focus on value‑added features and helping customers close new business sooner.
#### Implementation Overview
  * Embedded thousands of CrewAI agents behind the scenes of Gelato Connect to auto‑map bulk product catalogs and validate file uploads.
  * Deployed logistics agents that generate, test, and deploy carrier‑integration code, shrinking onboarding from 5 days to 10 minutes.
  * Rolled out internal “Crews” for routine ops tasks, multiplying individual productivity. ​


Early agent deployments slashed SKU‑mapping timelines by >90 % and cut carrier‑integration effort by ~99 %, enabling printers to accept new customers sooner and Gelato to accelerate global coverage—all without proportional increases in headcount. ​

## Brickell Digital scales Lead-Gen using Agents
Efficiency Gains
> _We’ve been able to increase the amount of qualified leads that we have coming into our business by over 80 %.”_
#### Challenge
Brickell Digital relied almost entirely on referrals, leaving its small sales team without a repeatable method to discover and qualify new business. Manual prospecting could not scale with the company’s growth ambitions.‍
CrewAI offered a lightweight, flexible agent framework that plugged into Brickell’s unique data flows and automated prospect research without adding staff.
Using CrewAI, Brickell Digital built an autonomous agent that scrapes fundraising databases and VC networks, scores prospects against an ideal customer profile, and generates design‑audit insights plus competitive analyses for sales calls.
The agent lifted qualified‑lead volume by 80%, improved close rates through richer call preparation, and freed the lean sales team to focus on high‑value conversations—supporting overall growth from three to fourteen employees.
